name: choir
generatedComment: GENERATED by lua tools/bank/bank_build.lua --recipe art/music/bank/choir-recipe.json from the sources of art/music/bank/choir.manifest.tsv (lua tools/brood_choir/brood.lua); do not edit.
comment: The brood choir's bank (openspec/changes/demon-choir design §4): a second bank beside bank.json, loaded after it while the sample bank is switched on. brood: the formant-synth doom choir, vowel by velocity (oh soft, ah loud) x six roots, looped sustains; grunt: rhythmic shouts cut from ACE-Step takes, one nominal root (they are shouts, so their pitch is reported, not gated), syllable by velocity, two round robins; warcry: the long shouts the dive war cries play, same scheme. Sources: lua tools/brood_choir/brood.lua (art/music/choir/brood.json). Levels are our judgement, matched by solo loudness against the synth choir (plan/render-runs/demon-choir.md). Rebuilt to the bank-fidelity standard (adaptive-soundtrack design §12.11; demon-choir design §4.1): the sources are 48 kHz float mono with no clipped sample (no declip, no pick, no resample); each instrument is encoded at the lowest rate whose median magnitude SNR reaches 35 dB in the 64-160 kbps sweep (bank_audit.lua bitrate), at most 160: brood 128, grunt and warcry 160 (noise-like shouts, 34.5 and 33.8 dB at the cap); the hits get raised-cosine end fades (grunt 0.15 s, warcry 0.6 s); the Opus budget rises to 800 kB.

local/brood-synth.credit: Brood choir: formant synthesis by the Demon Attack project (tools/brood_choir)

local/acestep-picks.credit: Grunts and war cries rendered with ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT) in the project's studio

instruments.why: rendered at each root, so the strict pitch check confirms the synth's tuning; oh/ah by velocity is the vowel axis

shouts, not sung notes: one nominal root, C3, the pitch the takes' clearest shouts measured (131 Hz; the take was asked in F minor). No pitch check: the shouts are short and noisy and a low drone of the take reads under several of them (plan/render-runs/demon-choir.md §3)

the long war cries, each at its measured pitch: cry_a F3 (173.6 and 174.5 Hz), cry_b A3 (220.1 Hz); cry_a_rr1 also reads the octave below (87.9 Hz, its growl); the score pitches them to the playing section's tonic
